population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: 2032 on 27.9 × 62% persistence = 17.3 stay on, 10.6 stop; off pool 9.1 + 10.6 = 19.7, of which 57% (11.2) restart → prior cohort on 17.3 + 11.2 = 28.5, off 8.5; new ever-users 11.8 (9.8 on, 2.0 already off) → on 28.5 + 9.8 = 38.3, ever 37.0 + 11.8 = 48.8, off 8.5 + 2.0 = 10.5 = 48.8 − 38.3; cycled 13.4 prior + ~5.5 first-time restarters among the 11.2 + ~0.4 among new starters = 19.3 / 48.8 = 39.5%. Persistence rose from 60% to 62% because prices fell again, HRSA access is free and unconditioned, and normalisation means stopping now has a social cost. Restarts held at 57%. Current users ≈ 103.4M of ~270M adults. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23%: 5.0 + 14.19 + 13.56 + 5.52 = 38.27 ≈ 38.3. The 65+ band rose 17→24 (~14.9M) as the dementia-risk label, Bridge renewal and routine antiresorptive 'bone cover' outweighed the bone wave and the Lilly DEXA scandal, which slowed but did not reverse uptake. 18–29 (16→25) grew through cheap oral starts, the gambling-disorder label, the readiness programme and police/fire contracts. Income thirds: (43 + 39 + 32.9)/3 = 38.3. Bottom-third use rose most (21.7→32.9) because the FY2034 HRSA expansion added free semaglutide for obesity at health centres, and Medicaid volume grew inside the existing structure. Most bottom-third users still take lower-efficacy product. Off-drug: ~28.4M adults (10.5%) have used and are off now. About a third of them were cut off by a missed condition (Bridge month-6 non-response, Medicaid lockouts in seven waiver states, employer BMI gates), and the rest stopped for GI effects, cost, pregnancy, the grey, or because they were done. Never-used: ~138M (51.2%). Most are adults who were never overweight and never had a reason. The rest are organised refusers (Open Table, fat-liberation, religious objectors), people with contraindications (MTC/MEN2 history, pregnancy, eating-disorder history), and the uninsured in the remaining non-expansion states, where cash prices of $149–219 are still a month's groceries. Under normalisation, even the lean majority of never-users are now asked to explain themselves. Pediatric: 1.8% of ~73M ≈ 1.31M under-18s, ~220k of them aged 6–11. The first pubertal-timing interim is still not published. Children born in 2029–30 are entering school having never eaten at a table where no adult was on a drug.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: extended in Dec 2033 through 2035 with the same structure and conditions (≥5% loss at month 6, ≥80% PDC, DEXA and resistance-training referral for 65+). Payment falls from $225 to $199/month from Jan 2034. The copay stays $50. About 5.2M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 5.2M × $199 × 12 ≈ $12.4B/yr. Medicare overall pays 14.0% of incretin fills ≈ 14.5M users (≈13.9M of the ~14.9M adults 65+ on drug, plus ~0.6M disabled under-65); the rest are on diabetes, CV, CKD and dementia-risk indications through Part D. Medicaid pays 12.5% ≈ 12.9M users at $199: 12.9M × $199 × 12 ≈ $30.8B/yr combined federal and state. The same seven adherence-waiver states (IN, AR, MO, OK, GA, OH, MT) remain, and none has been added or dropped. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program: the FY2033 CR held it at $5.0B. The FY2034 omnibus raised it to $9.0B, kept it unconditional (refill pickup only), and added semaglutide for obesity alongside liraglutide, cessation and AUD. It serves ≈7.0M: 3.5M generic liraglutide × $60 × 12 = $2.52B, plus 3.5M semaglutide × $149 × 12 = $6.26B, ≈ $8.78B. TRICARE/VA/DoD cover ≈2.9M, including ~210k active-duty members in the Metabolic Readiness Program: 210k × $139 × 12 ≈ $350M/yr. Under the Apr 2034 gambling-disorder label, eleven states let problem-gambling funds (earmarked from betting taxes) buy oral semaglutide for treatment-program enrollees, ~60k people: 60k × $149 × 12 ≈ $107M/yr, inside the cash/direct and Medicaid shares.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $6–35/month and generic tirzepatide at $25–60. Generic semaglutide is sold across Canada, Mexico, Brazil, China and most of Asia and Latin America. Retatrutide 12 mg was approved by the EMA in 2033 at European net prices of ~€250. Chinese originator triple agonists are sold domestically and in parts of Southeast Asia and the Gulf. US generic semaglutide is held up: the 2033 settlement entry dates passed, but FDA issued complete response letters to the first ANDAs in Feb 2033 over peptide-impurity immunogenicity comparisons and API-site inspections. Resubmissions are pending, with no decision before 2035.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~103.4M users: commercial 37.0% (38.3M), Medicare 14.0% (14.5M), Medicaid 12.5% (12.9M), HRSA free 6.8% (7.0M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 2.8% (2.9M), cash/direct 16.0% (16.5M), gray 10.9% (11.3M) = 100%. Managed decline continued. After the generic CRLs, Novo cut first to stay ahead of eventual generics, and Lilly matched under the Strategic Supply Agreement. TrumpRx/direct prices are $219 (semaglutide injection), $259 (tirzepatide), $149 (oral starting doses, unchanged), $329 (retatrutide, from Sep 2034, now on Bridge and most Medicaid formularies) and $279 (amycretin). List prices are unchanged: Wegovy $1,349, retatrutide $1,499. The high end is bimagrumab + tirzepatide (approved Jun 2033) at a $1,850 list price with no TrumpRx price. Payers cover it only for documented sarcopenia criteria, so most of its ~0.3M users are commercial with prior authorisation, plus a cash-paying affluent tail. Employer coverage rose 63%→65%, and ~55% of covering employers still attach conditions. The Sixth Circuit upheld PBM-adherence premium differentials in 2034 and the Ninth struck them, so plans in the Ninth Circuit states have suspended differentials pending a cert petition. Gray users rose to ~11.3M in absolute terms but fell as a share. Growth came from Indian-generic mail that slipped seizures and from 503A compounders serving people cut off by conditions. Skip-but-fill persists but is shrinking as dose holidays fall.

GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, Sep 2033)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)

reduction in risk of dementia in adults ≥55 with type 2 diabetes or obesity plus established cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, Jun 2032)

gambling disorder, moderate to severe, adjunct to behavioural treatment (oral semaglutide, Apr 2034)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Triple-agonist driver realised through an existing product: retatrutide 12 mg (30.4% at 104 weeks) moved from a premium cash and commercial drug to mass access. It was approved by the EMA in 2033, reached Bridge and most Medicaid formularies in Sep 2034, and fell to $329 direct. It now has ~9M US users. The Lilly DEXA disclosure (May 2033) added a hip-BMD table to its Warnings but did not remove the dose. Novo filed a BLA in Jul 2034 for a licensed Chinese-originated GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist (UBT251 lineage) on ~27% phase 3 data. Under the 12-month rule it is not on the US market, and a decision is due no earlier than Jul 2035. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide (filed Mar 2032) was approved Jun 2033, 15 months later, with a narrow label and a supply-limited launch. Amycretin (under review) was approved Sep 2033 at ~22% loss. Oral semaglutide for gambling disorder: the sNDA was filed Mar 2033 on a 52-week phase 3 (GD symptom-scale reduction plus ~30% fewer gambling days than placebo) and approved Apr 2034, 13 months later. No compulsive-shopping or screen indication has been filed. The incretin market is ≈$195B globally in 2034: US volume +36% over two years and US net price down another ~12%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Highest on retatrutide 12 mg and amycretin titration and among gray users who skip titration.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has ~78,000 filed and tolled claims. Bellwether record 4–3 for plaintiffs, and there is still no global settlement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis. Reserves raised again in 2033 annual reports.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases are rising with mass retatrutide access.
Registries still show low absolute risk with no causal confirmation.

A recognised population problem. In Medicare Advantage claims, sarcopenia diagnosis codes in 65+ users on drug more than 2 years run ~1.7× matched non-users. The gap is narrower among those with documented resistance training and protein counselling, and widest on HRSA liraglutide and compounded product.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings retained. Bridge requires a training referral. The FY2034 HRSA expansion added protein-supplement vouchers and a group-exercise grant line, but no condition. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide approved Jun 2033 for sarcopenia-risk users.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions are up ~7% from the 2029 trough. Modelled excess ≈ 14.9M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr baseline × HR excess 0.30 (down from 0.35 as bone cover spreads) ≈ 22,000 hip fractures a year, concentrated in women, cyclers and the over-75s. The Lilly disclosure (May 2033) showed retatrutide 12 mg total-hip BMD loss of ~2.9% at 104 weeks vs ~1.1% placebo. The original submission had emphasised lumbar spine. The final adolescent bone-accrual study (2034) confirms a ~0.2 SD lumbar z-score deficit after more than 3 years. Whether it is reversible is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Hip-BMD table added to the retatrutide Warnings (Jul 2033). Baseline DEXA for 65+ and postmenopausal women stays in class Warnings, not boxed. Pediatric labelling update (Mar 2034) adds bone-accrual language and recommends a baseline DEXA after 2 years. DOJ civil investigation of Lilly ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Denosumab discontinuation rebound and antiresorptive harms in 'bone cover' users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Users who cycle off the incretin often stop denosumab at the same time, and case series show the known rebound multiple vertebral fractures in that group. Rare osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fracture are rising in absolute numbers with mass co-prescription. There are still no trial data on combined fracture outcomes in 75+.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Endocrine Society advisory (2034) on transition to zoledronate before stopping denosumab. No FDA action specific to incretins.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort DXA data suggest regain after each stop is disproportionately fat, so repeated cyclers (~40% of ever-users) end lighter in muscle at the same weight. Conditioning cut-offs drive much of the cycling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. Cited in the Indiana waiver litigation and in HELP letters to CMS.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the BED, AUD and gambling-disorder trial populations.

Clinically meaningful anhedonia runs ~3–4% excess at high doses (retatrutide ≥8 mg: 8% vs 4%) and ~1–2 points excess at standard maintenance doses. Validated-scale surveys of long-term users put reduced pleasure at ~6–8%, down from 10–15% in open surveys, partly because measurement tightened and partly because affected users have left. Deliberate dose holidays in the past year are down to ~25% of long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed as 'uncommon' in the gambling-disorder label and as a class precaution above maintenance doses. The 2033 OMA/ADA 'lowest effective maintenance dose' guidance and Bridge rules that allow de-escalation without losing coverage reduced exposure.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still driven heavily by conditioning cut-offs. About 9M adults have been cut off by a payer condition at least once.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D signals persist, worst in the 30% calorie-deficit retatrutide population.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Bridge protein target; HRSA protein vouchers.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult and eleven of adolescent follow-up. ~220k children aged 6–11 on drug. Pubertal-timing interim still unpublished.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing; bone language added Mar 2034.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls are up ~10% with gray volume, mostly compounded dosing errors among people cut off by conditions.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CBP seizures continue; second and third peptide-distributor indictments (2033–34); no user prosecutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg. Absolute numbers are up with mass access.
'Brain health' prescribing to 50–64-year-olds outside the label keeps growing. They carry bone risk without proven cognitive benefit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label states population limits; no enforcement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Muscle spasms, diarrhoea and acne-like rash in trials. Long-term cardiac and hepatic data are thin, with only ~0.3M users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: REMS-free; postmarketing requirement for a 5-year safety study.

food_and_beverage.state: With nearly two adults in five on drug, US packaged-food volume keeps falling ~2.5–3% a year. Snack and confectionery brands sold to private equity are being consolidated or run for cash. Calorie-dense 'full' products now sell mainly through dollar channels and to never-users. 'Bone-and-muscle' protein formats are the only big growth line, and HRSA protein vouchers add a low-price government channel.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volume fall for a sixth year. AUD coverage and mass incretin use keep per-capita consumption sliding. Distillers rely on exports, ready-to-drink single serves and non-alcoholic lines. State excise forecasts carry an incretin line as a matter of routine.

restaurants.state: Half-plate pricing is the default at fast casual. Value chains keep closing suburban units, more slowly than in 2030–32 as the remaining footprint fits demand. Open Table suppers persist as a church-network niche. A few 'full plate' restaurants in Nashville and Grand Rapids market to never-users as an identity.

apparel.state: Size runs have restabilised around smaller centres. Workwear re-cuts are finished. Hip protectors, fall-safe footwear and 'posture' lines are mainstream in senior retail.

fitness.state: Prescribed resistance training is a payer-funded category. Bridge referrals, employer conditions, Medicare Advantage strength programmes and HRSA group-exercise grants feed low-cost gyms and PT chains. Strength coaches who specialise in incretin users are a credentialed niche.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend slows to ~+7% as net prices fall faster than volume grows. Plans keep conditions as the rationing tool. The circuit split on PBM adherence data has frozen premium differentials in Ninth Circuit states and left them in force in the Sixth. Bimagrumab combination prior authorisation is the new utilisation-management fight.

pharma.state: Lilly keeps national-champion status and tariff exemption despite the DEXA scandal. It has booked a $2.1B reserve against the DOJ civil investigation and a new bone track in the MDL. Novo is cutting price ahead of generics that have not arrived, and margin compresses further. Indian generic makers win abroad and wait on US ANDA resubmissions. US sports-betting operators report gambling handle per active user down ~6%, which they attribute to incretins.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on is unremarkable, like wearing glasses. Being off is what draws a question. Coworkers, doctors and first dates ask 'are you between pens?' or 'is it medical?' A heavier body is read first as cut off by a condition, and only second as refusal. A lean never-user is asked how they manage it.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: With retatrutide at $329 and on Medicaid formularies, thinness no longer separates classes. Muscle and bone do. The new top-end marker is the bimagrumab combination ('bima build'): a list price of $1,850, coverage only on sarcopenia criteria, and an affluent cash tail in Scottsdale and Naples. HRSA patients in Pueblo and the Rio Grande Valley lose weight on liraglutide and semaglutide with a protein voucher and a group class, and DEXA reports show the difference.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Most family meals now assume at least one diner eats a third of a plate. Open Table suppers in Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa continue but have plateaued, and the movement now speaks less of 'pharmaceutical fasting' and more of hospitality to the off. School nutrition staff in Columbus, Ohio, report children asking whether lunch is 'a pen day'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Listing the molecule on a profile now reads like listing a vitamin. 'Off' is what gets listed, with a reason: medical, Open Table, pregnancy plan. Dose holidays around conception remain routine, and holidays around anniversaries are fading with the grey.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is clinical, and in the gambling label it has become a template for every craving. People speak of 'my wanting' as a dosable variable: food, drink, bets, carts. The backlash still preaches that 'hunger is how we were made', but to smaller rooms. Montana, Utah and South Dakota joined Tennessee and Idaho in banning premium conditioning, framed now as privacy rather than appetite liberty.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Clinically meaningful anhedonia is ~3–4 points above comparator at high doses and ~1–2 points at maintenance doses. Validated surveys put reduced pleasure at ~6–8% of long-term users. Deliberate dose holidays fell from ~45% to ~25%. The 2033 lowest-effective-maintenance-dose guidance, Bridge de-escalation rules and selective exit of affected users explain the decline. Low-dose Foundayo for BED has ~1.6M users. Oral semaglutide on the gambling label has ~0.4M users, ~60k of them funded by state problem-gambling funds. Wellness 'quiet' subscriptions fell to ~0.9M.
interior_life.framing: A side effect a clinician screens for, like statin myalgia: the gambling label lists 'reduced pleasure' as uncommon. 'The grey' survives as a clinic shorthand and an older joke, not the national complaint of 2032. The therapeutic framing has won, and 'turning down the wanting' is how addiction counsellors explain the compulsion label.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers no longer talk about mood. Adherence still matters in Sixth Circuit states. Casino and sportsbook employers in Las Vegas and Atlantic City add the gambling indication to employee assistance programmes. Army chaplains report fewer 'grey' complaints and more about readiness tape anxiety.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' festival billing has faded as fewer people holiday. Comedy about the grey has become nostalgia. Sportsbooks redesign for 'casual' bettors with smaller, social wagers, and loyalty programmes report lower churn but lower intensity.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for anhedonia in a minority rather than presuming it. Couples still time conception holidays. Mismatched plan arguments now centre on bone scans and copays more than adherence windows.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The pro-access bloc owns the HRSA expansion and the Bridge extension. The backlash coalition has narrowed to religious objectors to the readiness programme (about 3,100 accommodation requests) and privacy advocates against adherence-based premiums. Asking whether a candidate is on has stopped being news. Asking whether they are off still is.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and price-managing. FDA approved bimagrumab + tirzepatide, amycretin and the gambling indication. It answered the Lilly DEXA disclosure with labelling, not restriction, and slowed generic semaglutide through ANDA complete response letters. Critics in India and Congress call that protection by review standard.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. Subsidy expanded inside existing channels: HRSA rose to $9.0B in FY2034 and now provides free semaglutide for obesity with no conditions; the Bridge was extended through 2035 at $199/$50; state problem-gambling funds buy the gambling-label pill; the DoD programme continues. The ACA cessation mandate is unchanged.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning remains the dominant access tool in Medicare, seven Medicaid waivers and ~55% of covering employers. HRSA stays the unconditioned exception, and health-centre staff now see patients who move to HRSA after being locked out of Medicaid in waiver states. The circuit split leaves adherence-data premiums legal in some states and frozen in others.
state.workforce_or_military: The Metabolic Readiness Program covers ~210k active duty plus Guard units in 14 states. Body-composition separations are down ~40% from the pre-programme baseline. About 3,100 religious-accommodation requests have been filed, ~70% granted with a waiver of the drug but not of the standard. Big-city police and fire contracts continue. The FAA pilot pathway is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 incretin duties stay in force. Lilly keeps its national-champion designation after the scandal: Commerce called supply continuity 'non-negotiable', and the Strategic Supply Agreement price ceilings were renegotiated down instead. India's WTO panel was established in 2033 and now cites the ANDA CRLs. Novo pays duty and cuts price. Chinese amino-acid export controls ease partially. The Global South runs on Indian generics.

events.event: FDA issues complete response letters to the first generic semaglutide applications, citing peptide-impurity immunogenicity data and Indian API-site inspections, so no generic launches despite 2033 settlement dates; Novo cuts its direct semaglutide price to $219 and Lilly matches on tirzepatide at $259

Senate HELP releases internal Lilly documents showing that a retatrutide TRIUMPH-4 DEXA substudy found total-hip bone loss nearly three times placebo, a finding the 12 mg submission underplayed, alongside a paid trainer-influencer programme describing the drug as 'lean-sparing'; DOJ opens a civil investigation, FDA adds a hip-BMD table to the label, and Commerce keeps Lilly's champion status
FDA approves bimagrumab plus tirzepatide for adults over 60 or meeting sarcopenia criteria at a $1,850 list price; CMS issues a narrow Bridge coverage decision tied to grip-strength and DEXA criteria

Year-end omnibus extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2035 at $199 a month with conditions unchanged and nearly doubles the HRSA Community Incretin Access Program to $9.0B, adding free semaglutide for obesity at health centres with no conditions attached
events.driver: state_action: subsidy; coverage_shift: status_quo; cultural_response: normalisation

events.event: FDA approves oral semaglutide for moderate-to-severe gambling disorder, listing reduced pleasure as an uncommon adverse reaction; within months eleven states authorise problem-gambling funds drawn from sports-betting taxes to pay for it

Retatrutide 12 mg drops to $329 direct and is added to Medicare Bridge and most Medicaid formularies, bringing two-year weight loss of thirty percent to public payers; Novo files a US application for its own triple agonist

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide is held back by FDA review rather than by patents. When resubmitted ANDAs are approved, HRSA and Bridge prices could fall sharply, undercutting the Strategic Supply Agreement that ties federal supply to Lilly. India's WTO panel says the review standard is disguised protection.

Lilly is under DOJ civil investigation and faces a new MDL bone track while remaining the government's designated supplier. Retatrutide 12 mg reached public formularies months after its hip-BMD data were corrected, and nobody has fracture-outcome data for incretin plus antiresorptive in the over-75s.

Use among people 65 and over keeps rising under the dementia label and Bridge renewal as the bone wave, denosumab rebound in cyclers and the cycling muscle ratchet accumulate. The Bridge expires in 2035, and its conditions produce many of the cyclers.

The circuit split on PBM adherence data for premium differentials is headed for a cert petition. Meanwhile HRSA, unconditioned and now twice as large, absorbs patients locked out by Medicaid waivers, and conditioning advocates cite this to argue HRSA undermines their incentives.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
Eli Lilly remains the Section 232 'strategic supply' national champion with tariff exemption under the March 2031 Strategic Supply Agreement.

prose.headline: A Hundred Million on the Pen, and the Only Question Left Is Why You're Not
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about a hundred and three million American adults take an incretin drug. That is nearly two in five, and almost nobody remarks on it any more. People in an office, at a church supper or on a first date no longer ask what you take. When they ask anything, they ask why you aren't on one. The usual answers are 'medical', 'pregnant', 'between pens', or, said a little defiantly, 'Open Table'.

Prices kept falling in small, negotiated steps. Generic semaglutide was supposed to arrive in 2033, when the patent settlements allowed it. Instead the FDA sent the first applicants complete response letters over impurity data and Indian factory inspections, and nothing has launched. Novo cut its direct price to $219 anyway, Lilly matched on tirzepatide, and in September retatrutide, the drug that takes off thirty percent of body weight, fell to $329. It is now on Medicare and most Medicaid formularies. A result that used to require surgery now comes through a public payer.

The way people pay has not changed. Employers, Medicare's Bridge and seven state Medicaid waivers still ration through conditions: lose five percent by month six, keep adherence above eighty percent, get the bone scan. What changed is that the free option grew. In December 2033 Congress nearly doubled the community health centre programme to nine billion dollars and added semaglutide for obesity, with no requirement beyond collecting the refill. About seven million people get their drug that way. Some of them were locked out of Medicaid in Missouri or Georgia and drove across a county line to a health centre that does not ask.

The bone problem is now a statistic people live with. Hip-fracture admissions among older Americans are about seven percent above their low point. The modelled excess is around twenty-two thousand a year, smaller than it would be because bone drugs are now prescribed alongside the incretin as routine. In May 2033 Senate investigators published Lilly documents showing that a retatrutide bone-scan substudy had found hip losses nearly three times placebo, and that the company had paid trainers to call the drug lean-sparing. The Justice Department opened a civil investigation. The FDA added a table to the label. Commerce kept Lilly as the national supplier, because the country runs on its Virginia plant. Weeks later a muscle-preserving combination was approved at $1,850 a month, and in Scottsdale the 'bima build' is what money looks like now.

The flatness people called 'the grey' has faded into the fine print. Doctors now prescribe the lowest dose that holds the weight, and the people most affected have mostly quit. In April the FDA approved a semaglutide pill for gambling disorder and listed reduced pleasure as 'uncommon'. Eleven states now pay for that pill out of their sports-betting taxes. Addiction counsellors call it turning down the wanting. Telehealth clinics extend the idea to shopping carts and screens, and betting companies report smaller wagers per customer.

The opposition has narrowed rather than vanished. About three thousand service members have asked for religious exemption from the Pentagon programme. Five states ban insurance premiums tied to adherence. Two federal appeals courts disagree on whether pharmacy data can set premiums at all. The Open Table suppers continue in Grand Rapids and Tulsa, smaller and gentler, and now speak of hospitality to people who are off.

One more change is easy to miss. A cohort of children is starting school who have never eaten at a table where no adult was on a drug, and some of them ask whether lunch is a pen day.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rosa Delgado clocks in at the community college kitchen in Pueblo at five-forty. The chili recipe still says forty pounds of ground beef, but she makes twenty-six, the way she has since spring, and still scrapes half of it into the compost. The students take a ladle and a roll and leave the roll.

At eleven she takes her break in the car and eats the protein bar from her voucher booklet. The health centre gives her the bars with the pen, a little cooler bag, and a sheet that says lift something twice a week. Her pen is semaglutide and costs her nothing. Last month the nurse said her DEXA showed her hip was 'a little thin for fifty-eight' and wrote a referral for a group class on Thursdays. Thursdays she works.

Her son Marco texts: Counselor says the pill is working. Three weeks no bets. The state fund paid again. She sends a heart.

In the afternoon a new dishwasher, a broad, cheerful girl of nineteen, eats a whole plate of the chili standing up. Denise from the register watches her. 'She's off?' Denise says it softly, the way people used to say someone was pregnant.

'Maybe she's just young,' Rosa says.

At home her husband Luis has made enchiladas. He has never taken it and never will, and his sister calls that his Catholic stubbornness. Rosa eats one enchilada and wraps the other for tomorrow. Luis eats three and says nothing about it.

After dinner she puts the pen in the fridge door next to the butter, where it has been for two years, and does twelve squats holding the counter, counting in Spanish so they go faster.
